unit.why: A single anecdote: the rabbi of Bar, travelling incognito at an inn, tests merchants who prayed hastily and is delighted by their defence of their prayer.

stories.start_quote: פ"א הי' לו במלון עלי דרך
stories.summary_en: At an inn, the incognito rabbi of Bar mocks merchants who rushed through their prayers by babbling meaningless syllables. They reply that God, like a parent with a babbling infant, understands his children even without clear words. The rabbi dances for joy at this defence and later uses it in his High Holiday pleas for Israel.

quotes: פ"א הי' לו במלון עלי דרך
tags.why: The story takes place while the rabbi lodges at an inn on the road.

quotes: ולא הי' שם במלון רק זוג תפילין אחת
tags.why: The setting is an inn, but no innkeeper acts in the story.

quotes: רצו להתפלל ולא הי' שם במלון
אמרתם כל התפלה לפני הבורא כל עולמים
tags.why: The merchants' hasty prayer is the subject of the story.

quotes: רק זוג תפילין אחת ולבש כל אחד התפילין
tags.why: The merchants snatch the single pair of tefillin from one another.

quotes: התחיל לרקוד ולשמוח בההמלצה הטובה הזאת
tags.why: The rabbi rejoices at the merchants' defence.
The parable of the babbling infant is central, but the merchants tell it, not the tzaddik.

quotes: בימי נוראים שאחרי זה בעת טענותיו
tags.why: The coda places his use of the argument in the High Holidays.
The tzaddik pleads before God on behalf of Israel.
The merchants take him for a madman until his point becomes clear.

quotes: והוא אמר אליהם מאַ מאַ מאַ וואָר וואָר וואָר
tags.why: He teaches his point through a playful, mock-mad performance.

missing_concepts: defence of Israel before God (limud zekhut / sanegoria)
simple Jews' hasty prayer valued by the tzaddik
